#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=petscDMDA
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks=4
#   --hint=nomultithread
#   --time=00:10:00
#   --output=petscDMDA%j.out
#   --error=petscDMDA%j.out

#flux: --job-name=petscDMDA
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 4
#flux: --time-limit=10m

# Omitted Slurm option: --hint=nomultithread
# Flux SMT/hyperthreading control is site/config dependent; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: ranks may be placed on logical CPUs with SMT enabled, which can affect performance/variability.

# Omitted Slurm options: --output/--error with %j token and join stdout/stderr
# Slurm's %j token (job id) and the "join" behavior are not portable in Flux batch directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames; stdout/stderr may be separated.

# Slurm variable $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is not set under Flux.
# Use the directory where `flux batch` was invoked.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

module purge

# Load PETSc environment
source ../../../petsc.sh

set -x

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, use flux-run to launch MPI ranks.
time flux run -n 4 ./dmda.exe -da_grid_x 1000 -da_grid_y 1000 -ksp_type cg -pc_type hypre

issues: The original Slurm script joined stdout/stderr into a single file. This Flux version omits output/error directives entirely, so logs will go to default Flux-managed locations unless redirected; consider adding `#flux: --output=...`/`#flux: --error=...` with non-Slurm tokens if you need fixed paths.

If the site requires explicit core counts for MPI ranks (e.g., `-c 1`), you may want to add `#flux: -c 1` and `flux run -c 1` to better match `--hint=nomultithread` intent (though placement/binding remains site-dependent).

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=petscDMDA       # nom du job
#SBATCH --nodes=1                  # Nombre de noeud
#SBATCH --ntasks=4                 # Nombre total de processus MPI
#SBATCH --hint=nomultithread       # 1 processus MPI par coeur physique (pas d'hyperthreading)
#SBATCH --time=00:10:00            # Temps d’exécution maximum demande (HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --output=petscDMDA%j.out   # Nom du fichier de sortie
#SBATCH --error=petscDMDA%j.out    # Nom du fichier d'erreur (ici commun avec la sortie)

# on se place dans le répertoire de soumission
cd ${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}

# nettoyage des modules charges en interactif et herites par defaut
module purge

# chargement des modules
source ../../../petsc.sh

# echo des commandes lancées
set -x

# exécution du code
time srun ./dmda.exe -da_grid_x 1000 -da_grid_y 1000 -ksp_type cg -pc_type hypre
